purpose: Measure quality/coverage of the existing SecondHopExpansionBuilder output (funder_upstream_links, creator_second_hop) at full scale. Candidate-only, no operation mutation.

discrepancy_disclosed.finding: 172 of 5,175 (3.33%) non-excluded bridges have total_sol BELOW the documented MIN_UPSTREAM_SOL=0.01 threshold from src/core/second_hop_builder.py
discrepancy_disclosed.explanation_attempted: the builder's SQL filters on ti.amount_sol (a single transfer's amount) BETWEEN MIN_UPSTREAM_SOL AND MAX_UPSTREAM_SOL, but funder_upstream_links.total_sol is a SUM() aggregate across potentially multiple qualifying transfers -- if a bridge has exactly ONE qualifying transfer at or near the 0.01 floor, total_sol should still be >= 0.01. The 172 sub-threshold rows are NOT fully explained by this reasoning and are disclosed as an UNRESOLVED DISCREPANCY rather than rationalized away.
discrepancy_disclosed.hypothesis_not_verified: possible causes not verified: rows written before a threshold parameter change, floating-point rounding at the boundary, or the row being written via source='rpc_backfill' (a different write path observed for at least one sampled row in P1.7) rather than 'transfer_index' -- NOT confirmed, flagged for future investigation rather than assumed
discrepancy_disclosed.action_taken: none -- this is a measurement/observation only, no code or data was modified to investigate or correct this

temporal_span_within_bridge.interpretation: the majority (66.9%) of non-excluded bridges represent a SINGLE observed transfer instance (first_transfer_ts == last_transfer_ts) rather than a sustained recurring relationship -- worth noting for future confidence weighting: a bridge backed by only one observed transfer is inherently weaker evidence than one backed by many transfers over time

self_loops_dust_mega_hubs.self_loops: not directly queryable from funder_upstream_links alone (the table does not retain per-transfer source/destination identity beyond the aggregate) -- P1.7's RAW relational transfer_index query (bypassing this pre-built table) is the only method that surfaced self-loops (3 of 9 raw candidates for the 20-member cohort), and that finding is preserved as the authoritative self-loop evidence rather than re-derived here
self_loops_dust_mega_hubs.dust: 172 sub-threshold bridges identified above; additionally P1.7's raw query found 3 of 5 genuine upstream candidates for the cohort were exactly 1 lamport -- both findings point to real, non-trivial dust contamination risk in upstream evidence

mega_hub_exclusions.top_example: AxiomRXZAq1Jgjj9pHmNqVP7Lhu67wLXZJZbaK87TTSk (131 distinct funders reached, 2.6x the 50-funder exclusion threshold)

fan_out_fan_in.note: these non-excluded top fan-in addresses are LEGITIMATE candidates under the current gate (2-50 funders) -- distinct from the mega-hub-excluded ones. They warrant SERVICE_DISTRIBUTION_REVIEW metadata per the B2Z-P3 policy even though they pass the volume gate, since 68-71 is close to (though under) the 50-threshold's spirit for a manually-reviewed case.

repeated_upstream_topology_cross_referen.finding: the top REPEATED_TOPOLOGY family root (5tzFkiKscXHK5ZXC..., 56 launches) from tf_populations does NOT appear as a direct-funder key in funder_upstream_links at all -- confirming P1.7's finding that the pre-built, volume-gated second-hop table has NOT yet processed this address's own upstream relationships, even though it IS itself a well-characterized structural root in a completely different discovery system (transaction_first_lineage.db)
repeated_upstream_topology_cross_referen.implication: the two local discovery systems (SecondHopExpansionBuilder and the transaction-first-lineage population builder) operate on overlapping but NOT identical coverage -- a future selective-verification pass should consult BOTH, not assume either is individually complete

measurement_method: bounded/indexed SQLite queries against database/flex_complete_database.db, read-only, zero writes
